factual_errors.text: Each fission event releases neutrons that trigger further fissions — self-sustaining if controlled, explosive if uncontrolled
factual_errors.correction: An uncontrolled chain reaction is also self-sustaining. In fact it grows, because more than one neutron from each fission goes on to cause another fission. The difference is not whether the reaction keeps itself going. In a controlled chain reaction the rate stays steady: on average one neutron from each fission causes one more fission. In an uncontrolled chain reaction the rate grows rapidly and causes an explosion. Spec: 'The chain reaction is controlled in a nuclear reactor to control the energy released. The explosion caused by a nuclear weapon is caused by an uncontrolled chain reaction.'
